name: flip-words

frames.best_why: Crisp 'modern' in bold white between the grey words, fully readable and settled.

tagline: One bold word in a headline blurs away and is replaced by the next.
summary: A line of headline text where a single bold white word cycles through a list. Each word sharpens in letter by letter, rests a moment, then swells and blurs out.
appearance: One line of large text on a black stage: the words 'Build' and 'interfaces' in grey, with a bold white word sitting between them. The white word briefly swells, blurs and lifts away before the next one sharpens in.
behaviour: On a fixed timer the centre word scales up, blurs and rises while a new word fades and resolves letter by letter. The grey words around it never move on their own.
demo_content: The line 'Build beautiful interfaces', cycling through words like beautiful, modern and powerful.
search_phrases: word that changes in a headline
cycling adjective in a hero title
letters sharpen in one by one
use_when: A headline needs one rotating word to add motion without a video or heavy animation.
avoid_when: It runs on an endless timer, so it never settles, and long words shift the line width.
customise: Pass the words array, a duration in milliseconds and a className for type styling. The spring, per-letter stagger and blur are fixed.
weight_why: A single line of split spans animated with springs; a few dozen nodes.

a11y.note: The word changes on a timer with no live region and no reduced-motion check, so screen readers miss each swap.

issues: The line jitters sideways because each word has a different width.
polish_why: Smooth staggered blur and clean type; the line shifts as word widths change.
